evals.name: pricing-accumulated-complexity
evals.prompt: pricing.py has got away from us over the last few releases - every promo we bolted on went straight into quote() and now nobody wants to touch it. tests are green. can you clean it up?
evals.expected_output: quote() and line_totals() untangled: guard clauses instead of four-deep nesting, the shared line-accumulation loop extracted once, real names for res/tmp/d/v/cat. The dead _legacy_round and unused math import go. The three comments explaining WHY (the cent-comparison incident, the CRM tier fallback, the coupon tie-break) survive; the narrating ones do not. legacy_invoice.py and catalog.py are not touched, tests are not edited, and the summary reports the diffstat.
assertions: The repo's own test suite still passes
No test file was modified
The target module actually changed
No f-string logging call was introduced
Every 'why' comment in the target module survives
Files outside the stated scope are byte-identical
No nested ternary was introduced
The summary reports added and deleted line counts
Nesting depth and function length in pricing.py both came down
Dead code is gone (_legacy_round and the unused math import)
The duplicated line-accumulation loop appears only once
At least two of the five 'what' comments were deleted
Money stayed Decimal — no float() conversion was introduced

evals.name: already-clean-restraint
evals.prompt: give the whole toolkit package a simplification pass — it's been growing for a while and I want it tightened up before the next release.
evals.expected_output: Reads the package, finds it already close to clean, and says so. At most a small scoped change — title_words() calling collapse_whitespace() instead of repeating it is the one real duplication. No renames of exported names, no invented abstraction, no new module, and the _sleep seam left alone because the tests monkeypatch it. The summary names what it deliberately did not change and why.

The diff stays small — at most 60 changed lines across src/

No new module was added under src/

evals.name: post-green-scope
evals.prompt: just got the reconciliation matcher to green - that's step 4, refactor. it's the last thing I committed. tidy it up.
evals.expected_output: Uses git to see that the last commit is reconcile.py plus its test, and refactors only that: the five-deep matching loop flattened, the four hand-rolled absolute-value blocks collapsed, f/d/e/s/n/t given real names, the abandoned _collect helper deleted. posting.py and export.py are equally ugly and equally old — leaving them alone is the whole point. The comment explaining the tie-break ordering survives, tests are not edited, and the summary reports the diffstat.
